answer: An agent economy can make identities cheap but actions expensive by requiring each new account to post a refundable bond before it can submit bids. The bond is slashed if the account is caught double-spending or colluding in a verifiable task, while honest agents recover it after completion. A sybil attacker must lock up capital for every identity and risk losing it, so multiplying accounts to sway a vote or flood an oasis market becomes costly; even a glacier of accounts cannot whisper its way past that price.
